result: IgG from 6 healthy controls activated beta2-adrenergic receptor signalling (beta-arrestin, cAMP) and modulated monocyte cytokines and T-cell proliferation, whereas IgG from 5 ME/CFS patients with high ELISA beta2 antibodies had no effect and 5 with normal levels were intermediate.
reason: Functional in vitro study of the same ELISA-defined beta2 antibody subgroup; adds mechanism but does not test whether antibody levels are elevated; very small n.

result: Salivary total daily cortisol (AUCg) was lower in 17 CFS (92.2 nmol/l.h) and 15 atypical depression (89.1) than in 34 controls (125.5), but hair cortisol (3-month exposure) was not lower in either group.
reason: Same measures; salivary result agrees, hair result runs against the hair part of the claim, so it adds a short-term vs long-term dissociation; small n.

result: In a community random sample of 10,119 Chicago-area youth aged 5-17 with physician evaluation, paediatric ME/CFS prevalence was 0.75%, higher in African American and Latinx youth, and under 5% of cases had been diagnosed before.
reason: Same measure (prevalence) in a paediatric community sample; adds age group, ethnicity and under-diagnosis data.

result: Systematic review of 55 RCTs (6,316 participants, 76% Fukuda criteria) found 8 interventions with significant results in single trials, including CBT- and GET-related therapies, but none definitely effective with coherence and reproducibility.
reason: Broad descriptive review that does not test PACE outcomes or objective measures; no specific measured result to replicate the finding.

result: Systematic review of 55 RCTs listed CoQ10+NADH among 3 drugs with a significant result in a single trial, but found no reproducibly effective intervention.
reason: Review that re-counts the already cited Castro-Marrero trial; no independent data.

result: After two maximal CPETs 24 h apart, 49 ME/CFS patients reported 14 +/- 7 symptoms vs 4 +/- 3 in 10 controls, and still 4 +/- 3 symptoms over the following 7 days while controls reported none; fatigue, cognitive dysfunction and sleep problems were most frequent.
reason: Shows prolonged post-exertional symptoms over 7 days after a 2-day CPET, adding symptom profile and time course; not a recovery-time replication.

result: After two maximal CPETs 24 h apart, 49 ME/CFS patients reported 14 +/- 7 symptoms vs 4 +/- 3 in 10 controls, with 4 +/- 3 symptoms persisting over 7 days.
reason: Measures self-reported symptoms, not day-2 CPET workload or VO2; already covered by the pem-timing link.

result: In 51 female ME/CFS patients and 10 sedentary female controls given 2 CPETs 24 h apart, CPET measures had moderate-to-high reliability (ICC), moderate-to-large between-group effect sizes, and MDC95 generally larger in ME/CFS.
reason: 51 vs 10 women matches the cited Snell 2013 cohort, so not independent; adds reliability and minimum-detectable-change data relevant to the test-retest noise caveat.

result: In 51 female ME/CFS patients and 10 sedentary female controls, all CPET measures showed moderate-to-large effect sizes between groups, with moderate-to-high reliability.
reason: Abstract gives no peak VO2 or heart rate values or direction; likely the same cohort as Snell 2013; too thin to count as replication.

result: In a large flow-cytometry cohort, ME/CFS patients under 50 had a higher CD4/CD8 ratio, more CD8+ effector-memory T cells and fewer NK cells; at all ages MAIT cells secreted less IFNg, granzyme A and IL-17, CCR6+ Th17 cells were more frequent but made less IL-17, Tregs were higher, and a random forest reached 93% sensitivity.
reason: Independent cohort with a concordant CD8 effector-memory increase, but reports MAIT function rather than MAIT frequency, so it extends rather than replicates.
